clue.text: Highly regarded part of speech on our education

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of speech, all of on and our, and the start of education

explanation.surface: Someone praises a school's teaching of grammar as highly regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' looks like a grammar term, such as noun; here 'part of' is the signal and 'speech' is just the first word of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To be honoured is to be held in high esteem, so it is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Recovered from illness, we hear, passed at higher level

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the phrase is to be judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: someone recovered from a bout of influenza is over the flu

explanation.surface: A patient recovers from sickness and is then promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that overflew a place passed above it, travelling at a higher altitude.

clue.text: Wrong subtractions standing in the way of enlightenment

definitions.text: standing in the way of enlightenment

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so the next word's letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad arithmetic stops a pupil from understanding the lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscurantist deliberately keeps knowledge or facts hidden, so the adjective describes opposing enlightenment.

clue.text: Tease bandleader about band

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
the leading letter of band
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Musicians mock their bandleader about the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is a narrow strip of material, which is one sense of band.

clue.text: Faculty head including article in study

indicators.note: including means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A university department head writes an article in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: In universities the head of a faculty is commonly titled its dean.

clue.text: Political group withdrew from house, partly

parts.note: to have left is to have withdrawn
a wing is one part of a large house

explanation.surface: A political faction walked out of the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From house, partly' does not hide letters; it means a part of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The left wing is the radical or socialist section of a party or of politics generally.

clue.text: Old material for writer it might make sense to hog?

definitions.text: it might make sense to hog?

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
ink is what a pen writer uses

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a pig would understand old writing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a grunt is the noise that would carry meaning to a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting noise a pig makes, so to another hog it might well communicate something.

clue.text: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats

definitions.text: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats

parts.words: Poetic device exemplified in Keats and Yeats
parts.note: surface reading: some literary technique used by those two poets
setter's reading: the two names themselves are the example, spelt alike at the end but pronounced keets and yates

explanation.walkthrough: One expects something Keats and Yeats both wrote with; instead the pair of surnames is the device on display.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the term for words that look as if they rhyme on the page but sound different when spoken, like love and move.

clue.text: Deter unity, ousting leaders for unlimited period

indicators.note: to oust the leaders is to remove the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to discourage unity by expelling the heads of factions.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is time without end, an unlimited stretch.

clue.text: Quartet playing that's regularly shown on TV

indicators.note: playing suggests the group is moving about, so its members are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the four points of the compass, a familiar crossword foursome

explanation.surface: A string quartet's performance appears on television every week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quartet' suggests musicians; here it is the four compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The news is a programme broadcast on television at fixed times every day.

clue.text: Creator of furniture, one seen in May, for instance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a craftsman who builds fine wooden furniture

definitions.text: one seen in May, for instance
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a prime minister such as Theresa May, who picks a cabinet of ministers

explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the month but is Theresa May, a recent British prime minister; a PM forms the government's cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a skilled joiner, and humorously describes any prime minister appointing senior ministers.

clue.text: Dunce securing prize thus for branch of science

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: an ass is a fool
a trophy is a prize
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quoted error

explanation.surface: Even a poor student can win an award in some science subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrophysics is the branch of astronomy studying the physical nature of stars and galaxies.

clue.text: Rearranged recital to include new instrument

indicators.note: to include is to take another element inside
something rearranged is put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A concert programme is changed to feature a new instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Tracks possible call as money's raised before match?

definitions.text: possible call as money's raised before match?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the two calls when a coin is tossed before a game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Money's raised' sounds like a bet; it is a coin flipped into the air, with captains calling heads or the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them, and the reverse face of a coin is called this.

clue.text: Popular judge imprisoning a holder of post needing to be dealt with

definitions.text: holder of post needing to be dealt with

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-liked judge jails someone holding a public office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holder of post' suggests an official; here post is mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is a desk tray where incoming letters and documents wait for attention.

clue.text: Singer dying for role in Tchaikovsky masterpiece

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bird of legend that sings only as it dies
second meaning: the heroine Odette is a bird in the ballet ... Lake

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an opera singer longing for a part; the singer is the bird of the swan-song legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the mute bird sings once before death, and the ballet's lead dancers play these birds.

clue.text: Team's method for event, not the main one

parts.note: a side is a team, plus the possessive s
how is the way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A team discusses its tactics for a minor fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a lesser attraction at a fair, or any subsidiary activity distracting from the main issue.

clue.text: Kind of drink with which one might get stoned

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spirit mixed with sugar and water

definitions.text: with which one might get stoned
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the strap weapon for hurling stones

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stoned' suggests intoxication after a drink; here it means being hit by thrown stones, as Goliath was.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore cocktail is one example of the drink, and David's weapon flung stones.

clue.text: Magnificent second place finish I had

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
the end is the finish
contraction I'd

explanation.surface: A runner boasts about a superb second-place finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means grand or superb, a direct synonym.

clue.text: I will be found thus in Pride and Prejudice, not Sense and Sensibility

definitions.text: I will be found thus in Pride and Prejudice, not Sense and Sensibility

parts.words: Pride and Prejudice, not Sense and Sensibility
parts.note: surface reading: some literary contrast between two Jane Austen novels
setter's reading: count the letter I in the title words; Pride and Prejudice each hold a single I, whereas Sensibility holds three

explanation.walkthrough: The novels are red herrings for literary analysis; the clue is about how often the letter I appears in the words of each title.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the adverb meaning a single time, describing how many times the letter occurs in each word.

clue.text: Turbulent ocean — it's damaged small boat's propeller

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the following word's letters are disordered
damaged means broken up, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Rough seas have wrecked a little boat's engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propeller' suggests a screw on a motorboat; here it is a person who paddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoeist propels a canoe, a small boat, using a paddle.

clue.text: Source for prophetic book who survived with pride

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the prophet behind a book of the Old Testament
second meaning: the biblical figure who lived through a night in the lions' den

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' sounds like self-respect; it is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament prophet gives his name to a book, and God shut the lions' mouths when he was thrown among them.

clue.text: Decisively winning point in court, usually? Excellent!

definitions.text: Decisively winning point in court, usually
definitions.meaning: first meaning: hitting a hard overhead shot to win a tennis point
second meaning: an informal word for wonderful

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash is a powerful downward stroke in racket sports, and the British colloquial adjective means terrific.

clue.text: More roguish fighter that takes a bow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the comparative of arch, meaning mischievous
second meaning: a soldier armed with bow and arrows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes a bow' suggests a performer accepting applause; here the bow is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means playfully knowing, so its comparative is more roguish, and a bowman is a warrior with a bow.

clue.text: Trousers seen after session — they're hard to miss

indicators.note: seen after tells us which piece is placed second, following the other

parts.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or parliament
ducks are trousers made of a heavy cotton cloth called duck

explanation.surface: Smart trousers are noticed after a meeting because they are so eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to miss' suggests conspicuous; it means easy to hit as targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting ducks are easy targets, so anyone aiming at them would struggle to miss.

clue.text: Type of gentleman's apparel, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word before it

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A description of the sort of clothing a gentleman wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the source of the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome, a gentleman's attire.

clue.text: Notice rising politician, moderate

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A newspaper notes that an up-and-coming politician is a moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a description of the politician but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp, as in damp down, is to reduce or restrain the strength of something.

clue.text: Flower-girl from nearby country, lacking finish

indicators.note: lacking a finish means losing the final letter

parts.note: the nationality of Ireland, the neighbour of Britain

explanation.surface: A girl who sells flowers comes from a neighbouring land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower-girl' looks like one thing, a flower seller; it is two definitions run together, a flower that is also a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloom is a garden plant and it is also a common female first name.

clue.text: Being over margins, needing to be reformatted

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: reformatting means arranging something in a new layout

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is upset about page margins that must be reset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning a living thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism is a living creature, which is what a being is in the noun sense.

clue.text: Drunken parties around area creating problem for host

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Wild parties are causing trouble for the person throwing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests someone holding a party; it is the organism a parasite lives on.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite feeds off a host animal or plant, damaging it.
